column3: “Decreed on her” is rendered “decreed against her.”
“Young men” is rendered “attendants,” and “good of appearance” as “beautiful.”
“Appointees” is rendered “overseers,” and “the house of the women” as “the harem.” “Into the hand of” is rendered “into the custody of,” and “rubbings” as “cosmetics.”
“Who will be good in the eyes of the king” is rendered “who pleases the king.”
“A Jaminite” is rendered “a Benjamite.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Beautiful of shape and good of appearance” is rendered “beautiful of form and face.”
“Into the hand of” is rendered “into the custody of.”
“Was good in his eyes” is rendered “pleased him,” and “bore favor” as “found favor.” “Rubbings” is rendered “cosmetics,” and “portions” as “food.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“To know the welfare of Esther” is rendered “to learn how Esther was.”
“From the end to be for her” is rendered “after the end of her twelve months.” “Balsam oil” is rendered “spices,” and “rubbings” as “cosmetics.”
“All that she said” is rendered “anything that she desired.”
“The second house of the women” is rendered “the second harem.”
“Said” is rendered “advised,” and “was bearing favor” as “found favor.”
“The house of his royalty” is rendered “his royal palace.”
“Favor and favor” is rendered “favor and kindness.”
“Made a feast” is rendered “gave a banquet.” “Tribute” is rendered “gifts”; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB adds “yet”; “in guardianship with him” is rendered “when under his care.”
“Eunuchs” is rendered “officials,” and “guards of the threshold” as “those who guarded the door.”
“The matter” is rendered “the plot.”
“The book of the matters of the days” is rendered “the Book of the Chronicles.” “On a gallows” may also mean “on a stake.”
